sentences.text: Arizonasaurus possessed a large back sail created by elongated neural spines on its vertebrae. This structure consisted of tall neural spines, a feature similar to those found in other basal archosaurs like Ctenosauriscus and Bromsgroveia.
The description of Arizonasaurus is based on two braincase specimens. The braincases of Arizonasaurus display some ancestral features that are plesiomorphic for crurotarsans.
The species Arizonasaurus babbitti was named by Samuel Paul Welles in 1947 based on a few teeth and a maxilla.
A fairly complete skeleton comprising about 50% of the animal was discovered in 2002 by Sterling Nesbitt.
Arizonasaurus belongs to the family Ctenosauriscidae and is closely related to the genus Ctenosauriscus. Arizonasaurus is classified within the order Rauisuchia and the unranked group Crurotarsi.
Newly identified pseudosuchian features suggest that ctenosauriscids like Arizonasaurus form a monophyletic group with poposauroids that is more derived than rauisuchians.

Arizonasaurus lived during the Middle Triassic, approximately 243 million years ago, in the Moenkopi Formation of present-day Arizona. Fossils of Arizonasaurus are found in the Middle Triassic Moenkopi Formation of northern Arizona.
